table: nav (K-P9-7: atx-equity-strategy-targets nav --list-rules --json, kind target, x-flag --target-rule mv-aim-v1)
citation: Menchero, Wang and Orr (2011), Eigen-Adjusted Covariance Matrices, MSCI Research Insight, May 2011 (cov-design section 8 source [2], https://www.top1000funds.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/06/Eigenfactor_Adjusted_Covariance_Matrices_May2011.pdf); Menchero, Wang and Orr (2012), Improving Risk Forecasts for Optimized Portfolios, Financial Analysts Journal 68(3) (source [3], its publication); Menchero, Orr and Wang (2011), The Barra US Equity Model (USE4): Methodology Notes, MSCI (source [1]); the alpha form alpha_i = IC sigma_i z_i is Grinold and Kahn's (strategy_spo.hpp, as spo-v2 defines it)
claim: a sample factor covariance under-forecasts the risk of its small eigen-directions, and an optimised (minimum-risk or max-Sharpe) portfolio loads exactly those directions; the eigen adjustment removes the bias, and the minimum-risk fully invested portfolio on the adjusted matrix realises lower out-of-sample volatility than on the unadjusted one (13.98 vs 14.64 percent annualised, US, 1994-04-15 to 2010-07-30, Menchero-Wang-Orr 2011, section Out-of-Sample Volatilities); a max-Sharpe target on the eigen-adjusted atx-cov-v1 store therefore holds the desired alpha at lower ex-ante and realised volatility than the desired target itself
source_sample_basis: read on 2026-10-06 in the text of source [2] (the URL above, PDF of May 2011): 'we select the 50 largest US stocks as of July 30, 2010 that have full daily return histories dating back to July 1, 1993 (a total of 4,303 trading days)' and 'the testing window is 4,103 trading days (from April 15, 1994 to July 30, 2010)'; the out-of-sample volatility test runs 'over the out-of-sample period April 15, 1994 to July 30, 2010'. Source [2] is the primary source (the paper whose construction the eigen adjustment and the optimised-portfolio test implement); source [3] republishes it (2012) and is not a later sample. Before 2015: not flagged under Ruling PRE-19; before the house window
predicted_mechanism: V^{-1} tilt lowers ex-ante and realised vol at equal gross alpha

constants_note: none: no IC, horizon, ridge, cap, clip or floor. A positive scalar on alpha (IC, 1 / sqrt(h), the desired target's cross-sectional SD) washes out under the gross normalisation (gtest MvTarget.PositiveScalarWashesOut); risk::FactorModel::create's specific-variance floor is not used (the kernel never forms F^-1 or a floored D: a name without a finite D_i > 0 is unpriced and keeps its weight)
fixed_choices: members M_d are the role's members at d; a NaN desired weight is no opinion (untouched, outside every sum)

priced P_d: members with a finite desired weight and a risk row at d (industry slot 0..49 and a finite specific variance D_i > 0, the names book_variance prices); every other member is unpriced and keeps its desired weight; nonmembers keep theirs

alpha_i = sigma_i x desired_i on P_d, sigma_i = sqrt(D_i) of row d; w = P V_d^-1 P alpha with P = I - (1 / |P_d|) 1 1' on P_d and V_d = X F X' + D of row d (X: intercept, the industry slot as one of 50 groups, 11 styles; K = 62)

V_d^-1 is applied as u - D^-1 X y with (I + F G) y = F X' u, u = D^-1 P alpha, G = X' D^-1 X, solved by partial-pivot elimination in fixed order: F is never inverted and the form is defined for a singular F (Ruling COV-13 (c); gtest MvTarget.RankDeficientFEqualsDenseSolve); I + F G singular (an F that is not positive semi-definite) refuses the run

gross (Ruling W3-17): the priced block is rescaled to the desired target's gross over P_d, so the priced block is dollar neutral, unpriced members keep their net and the vector's total gross equals the desired target's
pass-through, counted and never silent: no forecast at d, fewer than two priced names, a flat tilt (P alpha = 0)

refused before any compute: no store (--risk-model, --risk-model-sha256), anything RiskStore::open refuses (role, sessions, geometry, container root, seal), an industry slot of row d outside 0..49 and 255 (Ruling COV-11, S11), and with --rule spo-v1|v2|v3, aim-partial-v6, a rule other than aim-partial-v5, --two-speed, --adv-hold-q, --hold-band, --construction-grid (the row's incompatible[])

under --locate-in-aim the target can be negative on a special-tier name; no clip (no extra constant): the books' locate block still applies at the plan, and the summary counts such names (special_tier_negative)

the target is formed once per decision on the calling thread; every book (the capacity books and books on a pool included) reads it; a --calibrate-gross pass that forms the construction again repeats it and counts nothing
realised_leverage: Ruling C3-4: the rule has no leverage parameter and holds the target's gross at the desired target's (W3-17), so the book's realised gross leverage is aim-partial-v5's at the parent's L (or the L' of the PM6-6 match, C2); it cannot exceed a parameter of its own. Under a leverage rule the cap is that rule's (P9-MV names none).
